intro: You have arrived at Letoon Sanctuary, in Muğla province, a sacred place whose story runs from the 6th century BC to the 4th century AD. This Lycian sanctuary was dedicated to Leto and her twins, Apollo and Artemis, and together with Xanthos it is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
history: Letoon was more than a place of worship. It was the federal sanctuary of Lycia, where the religious and political decisions of the Lycian League were proclaimed. In the 4th century BC temples rose here to Leto, Artemis and Apollo. And it was here that the famous trilingual inscription of 337 BC was found, written in Lycian, Greek and Aramaic. In the Early Christian period the sanctuary was gradually abandoned.
structure-1: You are now standing before the Temple of Leto, the principal temple of Letoon, dedicated to the mother goddess Leto herself. This is the heart of the sanctuary that bears her name.
structure-4: Here is the Hadrianic Nymphaeum, a monumental fountain built under the emperor Hadrian. Pause for a moment and picture it in its prime, grand and gleaming.
structure-5: And now to the Trilingual Inscription, the important stele found at Letoon. It speaks in three languages at once: Lycian, Greek and Aramaic. One stone, three voices.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Temple of Apollo and the Temple of Artemis, the shrines of Leto's twins.
facts: Did you know? The trilingual inscription of 337 BC found at Letoon was the key to deciphering the Lycian language. Three temples stand side by side here, to Leto, Apollo and Artemis: a whole sanctuary dedicated to one family. And look closely at the ground — rising groundwater has flooded part of the site, so the temple foundations are now mirrored in the water.
outro: This brings our journey through Letoon Sanctuary to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Let this quiet place of the goddess keep its peace for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
